summary: Taliaferro County's first fire tower, dedicated in early December 1957 under the Georgia Forestry Commission; no source found on its later history.

events.note: Dedicated in early December 1957 as the county's first fire tower; no source gives a construction date, so 1957 is the dedication year

notes_for_editor: Current status is unknown. No source after the 1957 dedication says whether the tower stands, was removed or was moved, and no visit or access information was found. Height and construction are not in any source. The Georgia list gives the elevation as 605 with no unit, and no map site for this record was found to confirm feet, so the story gives the number alone. The parade detail comes from the magazine's account of the day; the newspaper item (dated November 28, 1957) only announced the parade. The tnlandforms page names no author, so its footnote gives the site name only. tnlandforms also lists a second, unsure entry 'taliaferro?' (GA315, 33.54833,-82.87851, marked 'loc?'), about 5 km south-southwest of this record's point; it may be the same tower. This record keeps GA197 because the 1957 directions (four miles northeast, or a few miles north, of Crawfordville) fit it. The newspaper spells the town Crawfordsville and the magazine Crawfordville. The 1957 built year is the dedication year, not a sourced construction date. The agency comes from the Eastern US Lookouts page heading and the magazine.
